Captured live through the mame server's own tools, by a one-off script outside this tree.
v30 (a MAME build carrying its driver) and m68k-dual, each booted
fresh and warmed up; `<board>-stop<k>.bin.gz` is a `memdump` of the scan range (v30
:maincpu 0x0+0x10000, m68k-dual :maincpu 0x200000+0x10000) at the k-th stop, 7 frames
apart (later stops further apart when a pair was trivial). `<board>-<width>-<op>.rows.*`
is MAME's own `cheatlist` after `cheatinit <width>` at the pair's first stop and
`cheatnextf <op>` at its second (`ub` stops 1-2, `uw` 2-3, `ud` 3-4), as sorted
`addr value` rows (value the current one) gzipped, or above 4096 rows their count and
sha256; v30's lists, kept only while its `overlay` control held, are of that
device, its dumps of the cpu. A stop's dump is kept only when its pair agreed with the
console. `mf-*` is
the two-filter oracle on m68k-dual :maincpu (three dumps, two lists). The console's own
answer to `save` is `<board>-console-save-answer.txt`.
Program and board names were then replaced by neutral labels by a single mechanical substitution
that preserves every field width; nothing else was edited.

m68k-dual's `cheatinit` admits every cell of 0x200000+0x10000 on :maincpu but the ones whose
first byte has no direct write pointer, the driver's own write taps (0x20173a-0x20173b and
0x20f8f4-0x20f907); `m68k-dual-<width>-not-admitted.txt` lists them, and every list and offline
compare of m68k-dual is over the admitted cells only (MAME's own `cheatnextf all` + `cheatlist`).
